headline: International Dark-Sky Reserve Access and Astronomy Pass
reservation: Daily access fees are mandatory through the Sépaq system, while specific ASTROLab activity and observatory tickets operate on a separate, high-demand booking schedule. Accommodation within the park, including huts and camping, often fills months in advance; always verify current entry quotas on the official site before travel.

days.title: Summit Ascents and High Altitude Views

stops.name: Mont Mégantic Summit
stops.detail: Trek to the highest point accessible by trail to view the ASTROLab observatory and panoramic vistas of the Appalachian range.

stops.name: Mont Saint-Joseph
stops.detail: Visit the summit chapel and enjoy steep lookouts facing the southern Eastern Townships valleys.

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes; mountain access roads may be steep and slow.
days.note: Summit weather is significantly colder than the gateway towns; allow extra time for steep elevation gains.

days.title: Celestial Discoveries and Valley Trails

stops.name: Sentier des Cimes
stops.detail: Walk through high-altitude forest ecosystems with interpretation panels explaining the local flora.

stops.name: ASTROLab Activity Centre
stops.detail: Engage with interactive astronomy exhibits in this dedicated dark-sky facility located at the mountain base.

days.driving: Local park transfers only; allow 20 minutes between sectors.
days.note: Evening astronomy programs require separate dedicated bookings and are weather-dependent.

days.title: Riverside Rhythms and Dark Sky Preparation

stops.name: Ruisseau de la Montagne
stops.detail: Follow the watercourse through the Franceville sector to see cascading rapids and rocky outcrops.

stops.name: Crest Trail via Franceville
stops.detail: A lower-elevation alternative offering views of the distinct rock formations of the Mégantic massif.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour if moving between the Franceville and Observatoire sectors.
days.note: The Franceville sector is separate from the main observatory entrance; check map routes carefully.

intel.title: Sector Specific Lots
intel.text: Parking is divided between the Observatoire and Franceville sectors; verify your trailhead location to avoid long detours. Spaces may reach capacity during peak autumn foliage weekends.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Interference
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly inconsistent in the deep valleys and Franceville sector. Download offline maps at the ASTROLab before heading to remote trailheads.

intel.title: Gateway Service Availability
intel.text: Fuel is available in Lac-Mégantic and Notre-Dame-des-Bois; there are no stations within the park boundaries. Ensure a full tank before ascending the steep summit access roads.

intel.title: Dark Sky Window
intel.text: Public observatory access is strictly managed via scheduled evening tours only. Day hikers should aim to be off the trails by dusk unless participating in an official night activity.

intel.title: Winter Road Conditions
intel.text: The road to the summit observatory may be restricted to shuttle use or closed to private vehicles during winter months. Always check the official Sépaq alerts for seasonal road closures.

plan.arrival: Pickup rental at Quebec Jean Lesage (YQB), source supplies in Sherbrooke or Lac-Mégantic, and check-in at the Notre-Dame-des-Bois park entrance.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable, but low-clearance cars should exercise caution on secondary park roads; check rental terms for unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Mont Saint-Joseph lookout for sunset, noting that descent in the dark requires preparation.
